content:
We have search results with three templates. Need the one that reproduces the Doebner modification retrosynthetic step for given molecule. The input molecule from previous step: precursors list from make_7_lvl2-apply_template-1 gave ['CC(=O)O', 'Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1'].

So target molecule is Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1 (an aryl sulfonamide with a side chain /C=C/CO). The retrosynthetic step should break the C=C double bond and the C-O bond (the alcohol) to give aldehyde? In Doebner modification, aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> alpha,beta-unsaturated acid after decarboxylation. Here we have product with alkene and alcohol? Actually product has /C=C/CO (allyl alcohol). The forward reaction would be aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid (COOH). But our target has CO (alcohol). Might be intermediate before oxidation? But we need template that when applied to target gives precursors: one is CC(=O)O (acetic acid) and the other is the aryl sulfonamide with aldehyde? Wait the precursor list includes CC(=O)O (acetic acid) and the same aryl sulfonamide but with /C=C/CO replaced by something? Actually the second precursor is same as target? Let's compare: target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1. Precursor list: ['CC(=O)O', 'Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1'] The second is identical to target. That seems odd; maybe the template applied gave only one precursor (the acid) and the other unchanged (the rest of molecule). So the template likely corresponds to breaking the C-O bond of the allylic alcohol to give a carbonyl (aldehyde) which then decarboxylates? Actually the precursor acid is acetic acid, not malonic acid. Hmm.

Nevertheless, we need to return the mapped_rxn and template_id (integer) for the template that matches this transformation. From search results, each entry has reaction_id, template_hash, retro_smarts_template, canonical_smarts_template, mapped_rxn, etc. We need template_id as integer (the one used to search the database not the hash). Likely reaction_id is the template ID? The description says template_id is integer. In search results, fields: reaction_id, template_hash, etc. So template_id likely reaction_id.

We need the template that when applied to the molecule reproduces the reaction (i.e., yields the precursors). Which of the three templates matches? Let's examine mapped_rxn strings.

First entry (reaction_id 440904) mapped_rxn: looks complex with many atoms, not matching our simple molecule. Probably not.

Second entry (reaction_id 104058) also complex.

Third entry (reaction_id 1325749) mapped_rxn: 'O=[CH:4][C:5]1=...' also complex.

Our target is simple aryl sulfonamide with side chain /C=C/CO. The template likely is a simple alkene formation from aldehyde and malonic acid? But the search gave templates with that pattern: retro_smarts_template '[C:4]/[CH;D2;+0:3]=[CH;D2;+0:1]/[c:2]>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[c:2])-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[C:4]'. This is a retro template: product (alkene) -> precursor (aldehyde + something). That seems relevant. The mapped_rxn for reaction_id 440904 includes that pattern. So likely template_id 440904 is the correct one.

We need to verify that applying this template to our molecule yields precursors: CC(=O)O and the same molecule? Actually the template would break the alkene to give aldehyde attached to aromatic ring and a carbonyl (maybe acetic acid). The side chain /C=C/CO would become O=CH-CH2-? Wait the retro template: product: [C:4]/[CH]=[CH]/[c] (alkene attached to aromatic). Reactant: O=[C](-[c])-[CH2]-[C:4] (aldehyde attached to aromatic and a carbon chain). That matches: our side chain is /C=C/CO (alkene attached to CH2-OH). Retro would give aldehyde attached to aromatic and CH2-COOH? Actually O=[C](-[c])-[CH2]-[C:4] where C:4 is the aromatic carbon? Not sure.

But given limited time, choose template_id 440904 and its mapped_rxn.

Extract mapped_rxn from result: It's a long string. Let's copy it.

Mapped_rxn for 440904:

'CC[SiH](CC)CC.[CH3:1][C:2](=[O:3])[N:4]1[CH2:5][CH2:6][CH2:7][CH2:8][C:9]2=[C:10]1[CH:11]=[C:12]([C:13](=O)[CH2:14][CH2:15][N:16]([CH3:17])[CH3:18])[CH:19]=[CH:20]2.O=C(O)C(F)(F)F>>[CH3:1][C:2](=[O:3])[N:4]1[CH2:5][CH2:6][CH2:7][CH2:8][c:9]2[c:10]1[CH:11]=[CH:12](/[CH:13]=[CH:14]/[CH2:15][N:16]([CH3:17])[CH3:18])[CH:19]=[CH:20]2'

That's huge and includes many unrelated groups. Might not be correct.

Maybe the correct template is reaction_id 104058? Its mapped_rxn also huge.

Third also huge.

Maybe the search returned unrelated templates because our query was too generic. We need a template that matches our specific molecule. Could use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching to test each template ID against our molecule. Let's try with each reaction_id.
